minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard fire and police FY19 requests; both chiefs urged more hires than the one position recommended.
minutes.summary: The committee heard department budget presentations from the fire chief and police chief. The fire chief sought five added full-time staff for round-the-clock coverage and paramedic service, and the police chief explained overtime, above-target items and the need for another officer. Residents spoke in favor of more staffing. No budget votes were taken, and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The fire chief asked for five added full-time staff for round-the-clock coverage and paramedic service; the recommended budget adds one.
The fire chief described paramedic revenue, payments to outside ambulance services and stipend savings as a partial offset to staffing cost.
The police chief said overtime is historically underfunded and is covered by moving money from other lines.
The police chief listed above-target requests, including a desk officer, clerical hours and supplies and training for a new officer.
Residents spoke in favor of fuller fire and police staffing. No votes were taken, and the meeting adjourned.

why_it_matters: Added fire and police positions would be paid from the town budget, mostly taxes, so the committee's choice between the recommended one position and the larger requests bears on the FY19 tax bill and on coverage and paramedic response times.
Overtime that is covered by moving money from other lines means the actual cost of police coverage is not fully shown in the overtime line.
